html:
The Saqqaq were the first known people to live in southern Greenland, from about 2500 BCE to about 800 BCE. They came from Arctic Canada, part of a wave of Paleo-Inuit peoples from Siberia and Alaska.

They hunted seals, caribou and seabirds with small stone blades, and lived in tents around Disko Bay, where the site at Qeqertasussuk preserved their tools in frozen soil.

In 2010 scientists read the genome of a Saqqaq man from a tuft of hair about 4,000 years old. It was the first full genome of an ancient human, and it showed that his ancestors came from Siberia, separately from the later Inuit. The Dorset and then the Thule followed them into Greenland.
sum: The Saqqaq were the first known people to live in southern Greenland, from about 2500 BCE to about 800 BCE. They came from Arctic Canada, part of a wave of Paleo-Inuit peoples from Siberia and Alaska.
